scope: RVW-001 and RVW-002: the invalidation receipt's in-process row law and its serialized boundary.

legacy_positive_only.identity: the pre-extension projection, byte for byte; every historical hash is reproduced

noncurrent.identity: the extended projection including both new fields

two_serializable_shapes.rationale: The owner emits the noncurrent schema only when at least one dependent is noncurrent, and emits nothing beyond the historical field set otherwise. So a serialized receipt that mixes the two shapes is an incompatible reinterpretation, never something to accept quietly.

from_dict_compatibility_boundary.rule: Any declaration of the new schema (the receipt_schema key OR the noncurrent_dependents key) must be COMPLETE and EXACT: the exact schema id AND at least one row. Anything else is legacy positive-only material.

outcomes.error: does not carry the exact ... schema id
does not carry the exact ... schema id

outcomes.input: exact schema id + empty rows list

outcomes.error: does not carry the exact ... schema id

outcomes.input: no schema key, no rows key (clean legacy)
exact schema id only, no rows key

from_dict_compatibility_boundary.additional_check: the reconstructed rows must agree with the serialized declaration about whether this is a noncurrent-schema receipt at all
from_dict_compatibility_boundary.embedded_record_ref_validation: RETAINED, and explicitly not treated as sufficient on its own

replacement_ref.why: That null IS the row's evidence that no lawful replacement exists for this dependent. Inferring it from an absent field would let a serialized row assert something the owner never emitted; dropping a non-null value would silently discard a forged replacement target.
replacement_ref.in_process_law_unchanged: NoncurrentDependentOutcome.__post_init__ already refused a non-null replacement_ref; R2 keeps that and adds the serialized-layer checks around it

in_process_positive_row_law.one_source_ref_maps_to: exactly one replacement row OR exactly one noncurrent row
in_process_positive_row_law.why: The dict assignment previously performed last-write-wins. With differing targets that let a caller substitute the owner's replacement successor, and the substitution entered the receipt identity and every downstream hash.

counterexamples_closed: two positive rows, identical target, silently collapsed to one
two positive rows, differing target, forged successor substituted
serialized negative row with replacement_ref absent, null synthesized
serialized negative row with forged non-null replacement_ref, value discarded
negative receipt with receipt_schema absent, accepted
negative receipt with forged receipt_schema, accepted
positive-only legacy material carrying new-schema fields, silently reinterpreted
residual_limitations: AuthorityInvalidationReceipt.from_dict trusts the declared schema only as a compatibility boundary; it does not and cannot re-derive whether the R/N/U partition is semantically correct from the receipt alone. That is the owner's transition law, unchanged by R2.

The schema-compatibility rule is deliberately strict: a receipt declaring the new schema with zero rows is refused rather than normalized. That is a fail-closed reading of HQ's 'incompatible new-schema fields/schema presence on positive-only legacy material must fail closed', and it is recorded here so rereview can disagree if it reads the requirement differently.
